strings.b-00-meta.title: Light – Reflection aur Refraction
strings.b-00-meta.objectives.0: Is lesson ke baad aap explain kar sakte hain ki reflected light kaise humein objects dekhne deti hai aur laws of reflection bata sakte hain.
strings.b-00-meta.objectives.1: Is lesson ke baad aap spherical mirrors, unke terms, aur concave aur convex mirrors se bane images describe kar sakte hain.
strings.b-00-meta.objectives.2: Is lesson ke baad aap mirror formula, lens formula, magnification aur power of a lens ka use karke New Cartesian Sign Convention ke saath numerical problems solve kar sakte hain.
strings.b-00-meta.objectives.3: Is lesson ke baad aap glass slab se refraction, Snell’s law, refractive index aur optical density explain kar sakte hain.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.0.definition: Ek image jo screen par form ho sakti hai; is chapter mein mirrors aur lenses ke liye, jab single mirror ya lens se tabulated cases mein banayi jaati hai, toh yeh inverted hoti hai.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.1.definition: Ek image jisse rays aati hui dikhti hain lekin actually meet nahi karti; yeh usual way mein screen par nahi mil sakti aur described cases mein erect hoti hai.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.2.definition: Ek image jisme left aur right interchange ho jaate hain, jaise plane mirror mein.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.3.definition: sin i / sin r ka ratio given colour ki light aur given pair of media ke liye constant hota hai.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.4.definition: Air ya vacuum ke respect mein medium ka refractive index, jo c/v ke barabar hota hai.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.5.definition: Ek convex lens, middle mein thicker, jo parallel rays ko converge karta hai.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.6.definition: Ek concave lens, edges par thicker, jo parallel rays ko diverge karta hai.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.7.definition: Lens ki power ki SI unit; 1 D = 1 m–1.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.8.definition: Ek lens jiska aperture uske radius of curvature se bahut chhota hota hai aur jiske do centres of curvature optical centre se equidistant hote hain.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.9.definition: Principal axis par woh point jahan principal axis ke parallel rays lens se refraction ke baad milti hain, ya jahan se aati hui dikhti hain.
strings.b-01.paragraphs.0: Hum kisi object ko dekhte hain kyunki light us par padti hai aur object us light ko reflect karta hai. Yeh reflected light, jab hamari aankhon tak pahunchti hai, object ko visible banati hai. Ek transparent medium light ko apne through jaane deta hai. Andheri room mein reflect karne ke liye light nahi hoti, isliye hum objects ko nahi dekh sakte.
strings.b-01.paragraphs.1: Light seedhi lines mein travel karti hui lagti hai. Light ka ek small source opaque object ka sharp shadow banata hai, jo is straight-line path ki taraf point karta hai. Hum usually is straight-line path ko ray of light ke roop mein dikhate hain.
strings.b-01.paragraphs.2: Jab light mirror jaisi polished surface par padti hai, to reflect hoti hai. Laws of reflection simple hain. Angle of incidence angle of reflection ke equal hota hai. Incident ray, point of incidence par normal, aur reflected ray sab same plane mein lie karte hain. Ye laws sab reflecting surfaces par apply hote hain, including spherical surfaces.
strings.b-01.paragraphs.3: Ek plane mirror aisa image banata hai jo hamesha virtual aur erect hota hai. Image ka size object ke size ke equal hota hai. Image mirror ke peeche utni hi door hoti hai jitna object uske aage hota hai. Image laterally inverted bhi hoti hai, jiska matlab hai left aur right interchange ho jaate hain.
strings.b-02.question: Inmein se kaun sa statement plane mirror dwara banaye gaye image ko describe karta hai?
strings.b-02.options.0: Yeh image virtual, erect hota hai, object ke same size ka hota hai, aur mirror ke peeche utni hi door hota hai jitna object mirror ke aage hota hai.
strings.b-02.options.1: Yeh real, inverted aur enlarged hota hai.
strings.b-02.options.2: Yeh virtual, inverted aur diminished hota hai.
strings.b-02.options.3: Yeh real, erect aur object ke same size ka hota hai.
strings.b-02.explanation: Plane mirror hamesha ek virtual, erect image banata hai. Iska size object ke size ke barabar hota hai, aur yeh mirror ke peeche utni hi door hota hai jitna object mirror ke aage hota hai. Image laterally inverted bhi hota hai.
strings.b-03.paragraphs.0: Ek curved chamakdar surface, jaise ki chamach ki curved surface, curved mirror ki tarah act karti hai. Sabse common curved mirror spherical mirror hota hai, jiska reflecting surface sphere ke surface ka ek part banata hai. Agar reflecting surface andar ki taraf curved hai, to mirror concave mirror hota hai. Agar bahar ki taraf curved hai, to mirror convex mirror hota hai.
strings.b-03.paragraphs.1: Reflecting surface ka centre pole P hota hai. Jis sphere ka mirror ek part banata hai, us sphere ka centre centre of curvature C hota hai; ye mirror ke bahar hota hai, concave mirror ke saamne aur convex mirror ke peeche. Us sphere ka radius radius of curvature R hota hai, aur distance (doori) PC equals R. P aur C se guzarne wali straight line principal axis hoti hai, aur ye P par mirror ke normal hoti hai. Reflecting surface ka diameter aperture hota hai. Hum un mirrors ko consider karte hain jinka aperture unke radius of curvature se bahut chhota hota hai.
strings.b-03.paragraphs.2: Principal axis ke parallel rays concave mirror se reflection ke baad ek point par milti hain. Ye point principal focus F hota hai. Convex mirror mein reflected rays F se diverge hoti hui dikhti hain. P aur F ke beech ka distance focal length f hota hai. Chhote aperture wale spherical mirror ke liye, R = 2f, isliye F P aur C ke theek beech mein sthit hota hai.
strings.b-03.paragraphs.3: Concave mirror ke liye, image object ki position par depend karti hai. Infinity par image F par real, inverted, highly diminished aur point-sized hoti hai. C ke beyond image F aur C ke beech real, inverted aur diminished hoti hai. C par image C par real, inverted aur same size ki hoti hai. C aur F ke beech image C ke beyond real, inverted aur enlarged hoti hai. F par koi image nahi banti. P aur F ke beech image mirror ke peeche virtual, erect aur enlarged hoti hai.
strings.b-03.paragraphs.4: Convex mirror ke liye, infinity par object mirror ke peeche F par virtual, erect, highly diminished point-sized image deta hai. Infinity aur P ke beech ka object mirror ke peeche P aur F ke beech virtual, erect aur diminished image deta hai. Concave mirrors torches, search-lights, vehicle headlights, shaving mirrors mein, dentists dwara, aur solar furnaces mein use hote hain. Convex mirrors rear-view mirrors ke roop mein use hote hain kyunki ye erect, diminished image aur wider field of view dete hain.
strings.b-04.caption: Concave aur convex mirrors: P pole hai, C centre of curvature hai, F principal focus hai, R radius of curvature hai aur f focal length hai. Concave mirror ke liye C aur F mirror ke saamne hote hain; convex mirror ke liye ve mirror ke peeche hote hain.
strings.b-05.question: Ek spherical mirror ka radius of curvature 20 cm hai. Iski focal length cm mein kya hai?
strings.b-05.explanation: Chhote aperture ke spherical mirror ke liye, R = 2f. Isliye f = R/2 = 20 cm / 2 = 10 cm.
strings.b-06.question: Aise mirror ka naam batao jo kisi object ka erect aur enlarged image bana sakta hai.
strings.b-06.explanation: Jab object concave mirror ke pole aur principal focus ke beech hota hai, tab image virtual, erect aur enlarged hoti hai.
strings.b-07.question: Concave mirror ke principal focus ki definition do.
strings.b-07.options.1: Principal axis par woh point jahan principal axis ke parallel rays reflection ke baad milte hain.
strings.b-07.options.2: Us sphere ka centre jiska mirror ek part hai.
strings.b-07.explanation: Concave mirror ke liye, parallel rays reflection ke baad principal focus par converge hoti hain.
strings.b-08.question: Concave mirror se bani image virtual, erect aur object se badi observe hoti hai. Object ko kahan rakha jana chahiye?
strings.b-08.options.0: Principal focus aur centre of curvature ke beech
strings.b-08.options.3: Mirror ke pole aur principal focus ke beech
strings.b-08.explanation: Concave mirror ke liye, virtual, erect aur enlarged image tab banti hai jab object P aur F ke beech hota hai.
strings.b-09.question: Hum ek concave mirror jiska focal length 15 cm hai, use karke erect image paana chahte hain. Object distance (doori) ki range kya honi chahiye aur image ki nature kya hogi?
strings.b-09.options.0: C ke beyond; real, inverted, diminished
strings.b-09.options.1: P aur F ke beech; virtual, erect, enlarged
strings.b-09.options.2: C par; real, inverted, same size
strings.b-09.options.3: C aur F ke beech; real, inverted, enlarged
strings.b-09.explanation: Concave mirror se erect image virtual aur enlarged hoti hai, aur ye tab banti hai jab object pole aur principal focus ke beech rakha ho.
strings.b-10.question: In situations mein kaunsa type ka mirror use hota hai: (a) car ke headlights, (b) vehicle ka side/rear-view mirror, (c) solar furnace.
strings.b-10.options.0: Headlights aur solar furnace ke liye concave; rear-view ke liye convex
strings.b-10.options.1: Headlights aur solar furnace ke liye convex; rear-view ke liye concave
strings.b-10.explanation: Concave mirrors headlights mein powerful parallel beams dete hain aur solar furnaces mein sunlight ko concentrate karte hain. Convex mirrors erect, diminished image aur rear-view use ke liye wider field of view dete hain.
strings.b-11.question: Gaadiyon mein rear-view mirror ke liye hum convex mirror ko kyun prefer karte hain?
strings.b-11.options.0: Yeh real aur enlarged image deta hai.
strings.b-11.options.1: Yeh erect, diminished image aur wider field of view deta hai.
strings.b-11.options.2: Yeh traffic ka inverted image deta hai.
strings.b-11.options.3: Yeh object ke same size ka image deta hai.
strings.b-11.explanation: Convex mirror hamesha erect, diminished image deta hai aur outward curved hone ki wajah se plane mirror se zyada area dikhata hai.
strings.b-12.paragraphs.0: Ray diagram ki madad se aap image ka location bina har ray draw kiye pata kar sakte hain. Ek extended object ko kai point sources maana ja sakta hai, aur har point kai rays bhejta hai. Clarity ke liye, hum koi bhi do rays chunte hain jinki reflection ke baad direction aasani se pata ho. Jis point par kam se kam do reflected rays milti hain, ya milti hui lagti hain, wahi image position deta hai.
strings.b-12.paragraphs.1: Concave mirror ke liye, principal axis ke parallel ek ray reflection ke baad F se guzarti hai. Convex mirror ke liye, wahi ray F se diverge hoti hui lagti hai. Concave mirror ke F se guzarne wali ray, ya convex mirror ke F ki taraf directed ray, reflection ke baad principal axis ke parallel nikalti hai.
strings.b-12.paragraphs.2: Concave mirror ke C se guzarne wali ray, ya convex mirror ke C ki taraf directed ray, same path par wapas reflect hoti hai. Aisa isliye hota hai kyunki ray reflecting surface ke normal ke along padti hai. Pole P par obliquely incident ray obliquely reflect hoti hai, laws of reflection ka palan karte hue aur principal axis ke saath equal angles banati hai.
strings.b-12.paragraphs.3: Har case mein, point of incidence par laws of reflection follow hote hain: angle of reflection, angle of incidence ke barabar hota hai. Aap in ray rules mein se koi bhi do use kar sakte hain diye gaye object position ke liye image draw karne ke liye.
strings.b-13.question: Concave mirror ke centre of curvature se pass hone wali ray reflect hokar kaise jaati hai?
strings.b-13.options.3: Principal axis se 90° ke angle par
strings.b-13.explanation: Ray point of incidence par reflecting surface ke normal ke along padti hai, isliye same path par wapas reflect hoti hai.
strings.b-14.paragraphs.0: Mirror equations use karne ke liye, hum New Cartesian Sign Convention follow karte hain. Pole P origin hai, aur principal axis x-axis hai. Object hamesha mirror ke left side par rakha jaata hai, isliye light left se mirror par girti hai. P ke right side measure ki gayi distance (doori) positive hoti hai, aur left ki distance (doori) negative hoti hai. Principal axis ke upar measure ki gayi distance (doori) positive hoti hai, aur neeche wali negative hoti hai.
strings.b-14.paragraphs.1: Object distance u hai, image distance v hai, aur focal length f hai. Mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f hai. Yeh sab situations mein, sab spherical mirrors ke liye aur sab object positions ke liye valid hai. Solve karne se pehle aapko u, v aur f ke signs sahi tarah put karne honge.
strings.b-14.paragraphs.2: Magnification m batata hai ki image object ke comparison mein kitni badi hai. Yeh m = h'/h hai, jahan h object height hai aur h' image height hai. Yeh m = -v/u bhi hai. m ka negative value real image indicate karta hai, aur positive value virtual image indicate karta hai. Object ki height positive li jaati hai kyunki woh principal axis ke upar hai. Image height virtual image ke liye positive hoti hai aur real image ke liye negative hoti hai.
strings.b-15.problem: Ek automobile ke rear-view ke liye use hone wala convex mirror ki radius of curvature 3.00 m hai. Agar ek bus is mirror se 5.00 m par located hai, to image ki position, nature aur size find karo.
strings.b-15.steps.0.title: Diye gaye values ko signs ke saath likho
strings.b-15.steps.0.detail: R = +3.00 m. Object distance u = –5.00 m. Convex mirror ke liye principal focus mirror ke peeche hota hai, isliye f = R/2 = +3.00 m / 2 = +1.50 m.
strings.b-15.steps.1.title: Mirror formula use karo
strings.b-15.steps.2.title: v calculate karo
strings.b-15.steps.3.title: Magnification calculate karo
strings.b-15.steps.3.detail: m = –v/u = –(1.15 m)/(–5.00 m) = +0.23. Positive m ka matlab virtual, erect image hai, aur size 0.23 ke factor se chhota hai.
strings.b-15.answer: Image mirror ke peeche 1.15 m par hai. Yeh virtual, erect hai aur object se 0.23 ke factor se chhota hai.
strings.b-16.problem: Ek object, jiska size 4.0 cm hai, focal length 15.0 cm wale concave mirror ke samne 25.0 cm par rakha gaya hai. Sharp image paane ke liye screen ko mirror se kitni distance par rakha jana chahiye? Image ki nature aur size find karo.
strings.b-16.steps.0.title: Given values ko signs ke saath likho
strings.b-16.steps.0.detail: Object height h = +4.0 cm. Object distance u = –25.0 cm. Concave mirror ke liye f = –15.0 cm. Humein v aur h' nikalna hai.
strings.b-16.steps.1.title: Mirror formula use karo
strings.b-16.steps.2.title: v calculate karo
strings.b-16.steps.2.detail: 1/v = (–5.0 + 3.0)/75.0 = –2.0/75.0, toh v = –37.5 cm. Screen ko mirror ke samne 37.5 cm par rakha jana chahiye. Image real hai.
strings.b-16.steps.3.title: Image height calculate karo
strings.b-16.steps.3.detail: m = h'/h = –v/u, toh h' = –v h/u = –(–37.5 cm)(+4.0 cm)/(–25.0 cm) = –6.0 cm. Image inverted aur enlarged hai.
strings.b-16.answer: Screen ko mirror ke samne 37.5 cm par rakha jana chahiye. Image real, inverted aur 6.0 cm tall hai, isliye ye enlarged hai.
strings.b-17.question: Ek convex mirror ki focal length find karo jiska radius of curvature 32 cm hai. Answer cm mein do.
strings.b-17.explanation: Chhote aperture wale spherical mirror ke liye, R = 2f. Isliye f = R/2 = 32 cm / 2 = 16 cm.
strings.b-18.question: Ek concave mirror kisi object ka, jo uske saamne 10 cm par rakha hai, teen guna magnified real image banata hai. Image mirror se kitni door hai, cm mein?
strings.b-18.explanation: Real image ka magnification negative hota hai. m = –v/u = –3, jahan u = –10 cm. Isliye –v/(–10) = –3, yaani v = –30 cm. Image mirror ke saamne 30 cm par hai.
strings.b-19.question: Ek object convex mirror se 10 cm ki distance (doori) par rakha hai, jiska focal length 15 cm hai. Image distance cm mein find karo.
strings.b-19.explanation: u = –10 cm aur f = +15 cm leke 1/v + 1/u = 1/f use karo. 1/v = 1/15 + 1/10 = 1/6, isliye v = +6 cm. Image mirror ke peeche 6 cm par hai.
strings.b-20.question: 7.0 cm size ka ek object concave mirror ke samne 27 cm par rakha gaya hai, jiska focal length 18 cm hai. Sharp focussed image paane ke liye screen ko mirror se kitni distance (doori) par, cm mein, rakha jaye?
strings.b-20.explanation: u = –27 cm, f = –18 cm. 1/v = 1/f – 1/u = –1/18 + 1/27 = –1/54, isliye v = –54 cm. Screen mirror ke samne 54 cm par rakhi jati hai.
strings.b-21.paragraphs.0: Light ek transparent medium mein straight lines mein travel karti hai, lekin jab wo kisi doosre transparent medium mein obliquely enter karti hai to uski direction badal sakti hai. Is direction change ko refraction of light kehte hain. Iske examples tab dikhte hain jab pond ka bottom raised dikhta hai, glass slab ke neeche ke letters raised dikhte hain, paani mein partly doobi pencil displaced dikhti hai, aur paani mein rakha lemon sides se bigger dikhta hai.
strings.b-21.paragraphs.1: Ek rectangular glass slab mein, light ray do surfaces par direction badalti hai. Air-glass surface par ye rarer medium se denser medium mein jaati hai aur normal ki taraf bend karti hai. Glass-air surface par ye denser medium se rarer medium mein jaati hai aur normal se away bend karti hai.
strings.b-21.paragraphs.2: Emergent ray incident ray ke parallel hoti hai. Aisa isliye hota hai kyunki do opposite parallel faces par bending equal aur opposite hoti hai. Ray thodi sideward shift hoti hai, lekin uski direction original direction ke parallel hi rehti hai.
strings.b-22.caption: Rectangular glass slab se refraction: air-glass surface par ray normal ki taraf bend hoti hai aur glass-air surface par normal se door bend hoti hai. Emergent ray incident ray ke parallel hoti hai.
strings.b-23.question: Glass tumbler mein paani mein aadhi doobi pencil interface par displaced dikhti hai. Kyun?
strings.b-23.options.0: Kyunki interface par light reflected hoti hai
strings.b-23.options.1: Kyunki interface par light refracted hoti hai
strings.b-23.options.2: Kyunki pencil paani mein actually bend hoti hai
strings.b-23.options.3: Kyunki paani saari light absorb karta hai
strings.b-23.explanation: Paani ke andar wale pencil ke hisse se aap tak pahunchne wali light refraction ki wajah se alag direction se aati dikhti hai.
strings.b-24.question: Rectangular glass slab se nikalne wale emergent ray ke baare mein kya sach hai?
strings.b-24.options.0: Yeh incident ray ke perpendicular hota hai.
strings.b-24.options.1: Yeh incident ray ke parallel hota hai aur sideward shifted hota hai.
strings.b-24.options.2: Yeh permanently incident direction se away bend ho jata hai.
strings.b-24.options.3: Yeh same path par wapas aa jata hai.
strings.b-24.explanation: Do opposite parallel faces par bending equal aur opposite hoti hai, isliye emergent ray incident ray ke parallel hota hai lekin sideward shifted hota hai.
strings.b-25.paragraphs.0: Refraction do laws ko follow karta hai. First, incident ray, refracted ray aur point of incidence par normal — ye sab same plane mein hote hain. Second, kisi given colour ke light aur given pair of media ke liye angle of incidence ke sine ka angle of refraction ke sine se ratio constant hota hai. Yahi Snell’s law hai, aur ye 0 < i < 90° ke liye true hai.
strings.b-25.paragraphs.1: Is constant ko first medium ke respect mein second medium ka refractive index kaha jata hai. Agar light medium 1 se medium 2 mein jati hai, aur uski speed (chaal) v1 aur v2 hain, to n21 = v1/v2. Medium 2 ke respect mein medium 1 ka refractive index n12 = v2/v1 hota hai.
strings.b-25.paragraphs.2: Agar medium 1 air ya vacuum hai, to refractive index ko absolute refractive index kaha jata hai. Ye n = c/v hai, jahan c air mein light ki speed hai aur v medium mein speed hai. Light vacuum mein sabse tez travel karti hai, jiski speed 3 × 10^8 m s–1 hai. Air mein ye sirf thodi hi kam hoti hai aur glass ya water mein kaafi kam ho jati hai.
strings.b-25.paragraphs.3: Larger refractive index wala medium optically denser hota hai, aur lower refractive index wala medium optically rarer hota hai. Light rarer medium mein zyada tez chalti hai. Rarer se denser ki taraf jane wali ray slow ho jati hai aur normal ki taraf bend karti hai; denser se rarer ki taraf jane wali ray speed up ho jati hai aur normal se door bend karti hai. Optical density mass density ke same nahin hoti: kerosene ka refractive index water se higher hai, isliye ye water se optically denser hai, although iski mass density kam hai.
strings.b-26.question: Hawa mein chal rahi light ki ek ray tirchhi (obliquely) paani mein pravesh karti hai. Kya ye normal (abhilamb) ki taraf mudti hai ya normal se door, aur kyun?
strings.b-26.options.0: Normal ki taraf, kyunki paani hawa se optically denser hai.
strings.b-26.options.1: Normal se door, kyunki paani hawa se optically rarer hai.
strings.b-26.options.2: Ye bina mude seedha chali jaati hai.
strings.b-26.options.3: Ye normal ki taraf mudti hai kyunki paani ka refractive index kam hai.
strings.b-26.explanation: Paani ka refractive index hawa se zyada hota hai, isliye ye optically denser hai. Rarer se denser medium mein jaane wali ray slow hoti hai aur normal ki taraf mudti hai.
strings.b-27.question: Light air se glass mein pravesh karti hai jiska refractive index 1.50 hai. Vacuum mein light ki speed (chaal) 3 × 10^8 m/s hai. Glass mein light ki speed m/s mein kya hai?
strings.b-28.question: Refractive index table se, kaun sa medium sabse zyada optical density rakhta hai aur kaun sa sabse kam?
strings.b-28.options.0: Diamond mein sabse zyada hai; air mein sabse kam hai.
strings.b-28.options.1: Air mein sabse zyada hai; diamond mein sabse kam hai.
strings.b-28.options.2: Water mein sabse zyada hai; kerosene mein sabse kam hai.
strings.b-28.options.3: Crown glass mein sabse zyada hai; water mein sabse kam hai.
strings.b-28.explanation: Diamond ka refractive index 2.42 hai, jo listed sabse bada hai, aur air ka 1.0003 hai, jo listed sabse chhota hai. Bada refractive index optically denser hone ka matlab hai.
strings.b-29.question: Aapko kerosene, turpentine aur water diye gaye hain. Inmein se kis mein light sabse tez travel karti hai?
strings.b-29.explanation: Water ka refractive index in teeno mein sabse chhota hai (1.33, kerosene ke 1.44 aur turpentine ke 1.47 ke mukable), isliye light water mein sabse tez travel karti hai.
strings.b-30.question: Diamond ka refractive index 2.42 hai. Is statement ka kya matlab hai?
strings.b-30.options.0: Air mein light ki speed (chaal) aur diamond mein light ki speed ka ratio 2.42 hai, isliye diamond mein light dheemi hoti hai.
strings.b-30.options.1: Diamond mein light ki speed (chaal) aur air mein light ki speed ka ratio 2.42 hai.
strings.b-30.options.2: Light diamond mein air se zyada tez travel karti hai.
strings.b-30.options.3: Diamond ki mass density air se 2.42 guna hai.
strings.b-30.explanation: Absolute refractive index ke liye, n = c/v. Value 2.42 ka matlab hai ki c, diamond mein light ki speed (chaal) ka 2.42 guna hai.
strings.b-31.paragraphs.0: A lens ek transparent material hai jo do surfaces se bound hota hai, jinme se ek ya dono spherical hote hain. Convex lens middle mein edges se thicker hota hai, aur light rays ko converge karta hai, isliye yeh converging lens hai. Concave lens edges par middle se thicker hota hai, aur light rays ko diverge karta hai, isliye yeh diverging lens hai.
strings.b-31.paragraphs.1: Ek lens ke do centres of curvature C1 aur C2 hote hain. Principal axis in centres se pass karta hai. Lens ka central point optical centre O hai. O se pass hone wala ray bina deviation ke pass hota hai. Circular outline ka effective diameter aperture hai. Hum small apertures wale thin lenses consider karte hain.
strings.b-31.paragraphs.2: Principal axis ke parallel rays convex lens se refraction ke baad principal focus par converge karte hain. Concave lens mein yeh same side par principal focus se diverge karte hue appear hote hain. Ek lens ke do principal foci F1 aur F2 hote hain, aur focal length f optical centre se principal focus ki distance (doori) hai. Lens aur Sun ke sharp image ke beech ki distance approximate focal length deti hai.
strings.b-31.paragraphs.3: Convex lens ke liye image table yeh hai: object infinity par ho to F2 par real, inverted, highly diminished point-sized image milti hai; object 2F1 se aage ho to F2 aur 2F2 ke beech real, inverted, diminished image milti hai; object 2F1 par ho to 2F2 par real, inverted same-size image milti hai; object F1 aur 2F1 ke beech ho to 2F2 se aage real, inverted enlarged image milti hai; object F1 par ho to koi image nahi banti; object F1 aur O ke beech ho to object ke same side par virtual, erect, enlarged image milti hai.

lesson.title: Light – Reflection aur Refraction
objectives: Is lesson ke baad aap explain kar sakte hain ki reflected light kaise humein objects dekhne deti hai aur laws of reflection bata sakte hain.
Is lesson ke baad aap spherical mirrors, unke terms, aur concave aur convex mirrors se bane images describe kar sakte hain.
Is lesson ke baad aap mirror formula, lens formula, magnification aur power of a lens ka use karke New Cartesian Sign Convention ke saath numerical problems solve kar sakte hain.
Is lesson ke baad aap glass slab se refraction, Snell’s law, refractive index aur optical density explain kar sakte hain.

sections.title: Light, reflection, aur plane mirror
paragraphs: Hum ek object ko dekhte hain kyunki us par light padti hai aur object us light ko reflect karta hai. Yeh reflected light, jab hamari aankhon tak pahunchti hai, object ko visible banati hai. Ek transparent medium bhi light ko apne through jaane deta hai. Ek dark room mein reflect karne ke liye light nahi hoti, isliye hum objects ko nahi dekh sakte.

Light seedhi lines mein travel karti hui lagti hai. Light ka ek chhota source ek opaque object ki sharp shadow banata hai, jo is straight-line path ko point karta hai. Hum usually is straight-line path ko ray of light ke roop mein dikhate hain.

Jab light ek polished surface jaise mirror par padti hai, toh woh reflect hoti hai. Laws of reflection simple hain. Angle of incidence, angle of reflection ke barabar hota hai. Incident ray, point of incidence par normal, aur reflected ray sabhi same plane mein hote hain. Yeh laws sabhi reflecting surfaces par apply hote hain, including spherical surfaces.

Ek plane mirror ek image banata hai jo always virtual aur erect hoti hai. Image ka size object ke size ke barabar hota hai. Image mirror ke peeche utni door hoti hai jitna object uske aage hota hai. Image laterally inverted bhi hoti hai, matlab left aur right interchange ho jaate hain.

sections.title: Spherical mirrors aur unki images
paragraphs: Ek curved shining surface, jaise spoon ki curved surface, ek curved mirror ki tarah act karti hai. Sabse common curved mirror spherical mirror hota hai, jiska reflecting surface ek sphere ki surface ka part hota hai. Agar reflecting surface andar ki taraf curved hai, toh mirror concave mirror hota hai. Agar bahar ki taraf curved hai, toh mirror convex mirror hota hai.

Reflecting surface ka centre pole P hota hai. Jis sphere ka mirror part hota hai, us sphere ka centre centre of curvature C hota hai; yeh mirror ke bahar hota hai, concave mirror ke aage aur convex mirror ke peeche. Us sphere ka radius radius of curvature R hota hai, aur distance PC = R. P aur C ke through straight line principal axis hoti hai, aur yeh P par mirror ke normal hoti hai. Reflecting surface ka diameter aperture hota hai. Hum un mirrors ko consider karte hain jinka aperture unke radius of curvature se bahut chhota hota hai.

Principal axis ke parallel rays concave mirror se reflection ke baad ek point par milte hain. Yeh point principal focus F hota hai. Convex mirror mein reflected rays F se diverge hoti hui dikhti hain. P aur F ke beech ki distance focal length f hoti hai. Chhote aperture wale spherical mirror ke liye, R = 2f, isliye F, P aur C ke beech mein lies karta hai.

Concave mirror ke liye, image object position par depend karti hai. Infinity par image real, inverted, highly diminished aur point-sized hoti hai F par. C se beyond image real, inverted aur diminished hoti hai F aur C ke beech. C par image real, inverted aur same size ki hoti hai C par. C aur F ke beech image real, inverted aur enlarged hoti hai C se beyond. F par koi image nahi banti. P aur F ke beech image virtual, erect aur enlarged hoti hai mirror ke peeche.

Convex mirror ke liye, infinity par object virtual, erect, highly diminished point-sized image deta hai F par mirror ke peeche. Infinity aur P ke beech object virtual, erect aur diminished image deta hai P aur F ke beech mirror ke peeche. Concave mirrors torches, search-lights, vehicle headlights, shaving mirrors, dentists dwara, aur solar furnaces mein use hote hain. Convex mirrors rear-view mirrors ke roop mein use hote hain kyunki ye erect, diminished image aur wider field of view dete hain.

sections.title: Mirrors ke liye ray diagrams drawing
paragraphs: Ek ray diagram aapko image locate karne mein help karta hai bina har ray draw kiye. Ek extended object ko many point sources ki tarah treat kar sakte hain, aur har point many rays bhejta hai. Clarity ke liye, hum koi bhi do rays choose karte hain jinki reflection ke baad directions easy to know hain. Jis point par kam se kam do reflected rays milti hain, ya milti hui dikhti hain, woh image position deta hai.

Concave mirror ke liye, principal axis ke parallel ray reflection ke baad F se pass hoti hai. Convex mirror ke liye, wahi ray F se diverge hoti hui dikhti hai. Concave mirror ke F se pass hone wali ray, ya convex mirror ke F ki taraf directed ray, reflection ke baad principal axis ke parallel emerge hoti hai.

Concave mirror ke C se pass hone wali ray, ya convex mirror ke C ki taraf directed ray, same path ke along reflect ho jaati hai. Yeh isliye hota hai kyunki ray reflecting surface ke normal ke along padti hai. Pole P par obliquely incident ray obliquely reflect hoti hai, laws of reflection follow karte hue aur principal axis ke saath equal angles banate hue.

Har case mein, point of incidence par laws of reflection follow hote hain: angle of reflection, angle of incidence ke barabar hota hai. Aap in ray rules mein se koi bhi do use karke given object position ke liye image draw kar sakte hain.

sections.title: Sign convention aur mirror formula
paragraphs: Mirror equations use karne ke liye, hum New Cartesian Sign Convention follow karte hain. Pole P origin hota hai, aur principal axis x-axis hoti hai. Object always mirror ke left mein place hota hai, isliye light mirror par left se padti hai. P ke right mein measure ki gayi distances positive hoti hain, aur left ki distances negative. Principal axis ke upar measure ki gayi distances positive hoti hain, aur neeche ki negative.

Object distance u hoti hai, image distance v hoti hai, aur focal length f hoti hai. Mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f hai. Yeh sabhi situations mein sabhi spherical mirrors aur sabhi object positions ke liye valid hai. Solve karne se pehle aapko u, v aur f ke signs correctly put karne honge.

Magnification m batata hai ki image object ke compare mein kitni badi hai. Yeh m = h'/h hota hai, jahan h object height hai aur h' image height hai. Yeh m = -v/u bhi hota hai. m ka negative value real image indicate karta hai, aur positive value virtual image. Object ki height positive li jaati hai kyunki yeh principal axis ke upar hoti hai. Image height virtual image ke liye positive hoti hai aur real image ke liye negative.

sections.title: Refraction aur rectangular glass slab
paragraphs: Light ek transparent medium mein straight lines mein travel karti hai, lekin jab yeh doosre transparent medium mein obliquely enter karti hai toh iski direction change ho sakti hai. Is direction change ko refraction of light kehte hain. Aap iske examples dekhte hain jab pond ka bottom raised dikhta hai, jab glass slab ke neeche letters raised dikhte hain, jab partly water mein rakhi pencil displaced dikhti hai, aur jab water mein rakha lemon sides se bigger dikhta hai.

Ek rectangular glass slab mein, light ray do surfaces par direction change karti hai. Air-glass surface par yeh rarer medium se denser medium mein jaati hai aur normal ki taraf bend hoti hai. Glass-air surface par yeh denser medium se rarer medium mein jaati hai aur normal se away bend hoti hai.

Emergent ray incident ray ke parallel hoti hai. Yeh isliye hota hai kyunki do opposite parallel faces par bending equal aur opposite hoti hai. Ray thoda sideward shift hoti hai, lekin iski direction original direction ke parallel rehti hai.

sections.title: Laws of refraction aur refractive index
paragraphs: Refraction do laws follow karta hai. Pehla, incident ray, refracted ray aur point of incidence par normal sabhi same plane mein hote hain. Doosra, angle of incidence ke sine ka angle of refraction ke sine se ratio ek constant hota hai given colour ki light ke liye aur given pair of media ke liye. Yeh Snell’s law hai, aur yeh 0 < i < 90° ke liye true hai.

Is constant ko second medium ka refractive index first medium ke respect mein kehte hain. Agar light medium 1 se medium 2 mein travel karti hai, aur iski speeds v1 aur v2 hain, toh n21 = v1/v2. Medium 1 ka refractive index medium 2 ke respect mein n12 = v2/v1 hota hai.

Agar medium 1 air ya vacuum hai, toh refractive index ko absolute refractive index kehte hain. Yeh n = c/v hota hai, jahan c air mein light ki speed hai aur v medium mein speed hai. Light vacuum mein sabse fast travel karti hai speed 3 × 10^8 m s–1 ke saath. Air mein yeh marginally kam hoti hai aur glass ya water mein considerably reduce hoti hai.

Larger refractive index wala medium optically denser hota hai, aur lower refractive index wala medium optically rarer. Light rarer medium mein faster travel karti hai. Rarer se denser jaane wali ray slow down hoti hai aur normal ki taraf bend hoti hai; denser se rarer jaane wali ray speed up hoti hai aur normal se away bend hoti hai. Optical density mass density ke same nahi hoti: kerosene ka refractive index water se higher hai, isliye yeh water se optically denser hai, although iski mass density less hai.

sections.title: Lenses aur unki images
paragraphs: Ek lens ek transparent material hai jo do surfaces se bound hota hai, jisme se ek ya dono spherical hote hain. Convex lens middle mein edges se thicker hota hai, aur yeh light rays ko converge karta hai, isliye yeh converging lens hai. Concave lens edges par middle se thicker hota hai, aur yeh light rays ko diverge karta hai, isliye yeh diverging lens hai.

Ek lens ke do centres of curvature C1 aur C2 hote hain. Principal axis in centres se pass hoti hai. Lens ka central point optical centre O hota hai. O se pass hone wali ray bina deviation ke pass hoti hai. Circular outline ka effective diameter aperture hota hai. Hum small apertures wale thin lenses consider karte hain.

Principal axis ke parallel rays convex lens se refraction ke baad principal focus par converge hoti hain. Concave lens mein yeh same side par principal focus se diverge hoti hui dikhti hain. Ek lens ke do principal foci F1 aur F2 hote hain, aur focal length f optical centre se principal focus ki distance hoti hai. Lens aur Sun ki sharp image ke beech ki distance approximate focal length deti hai.

Convex lens ke liye, image table hai: object infinity par real, inverted, highly diminished point-sized image deta hai F2 par; 2F1 se beyond real, inverted, diminished image deta hai F2 aur 2F2 ke beech; 2F1 par real, inverted same-size image deta hai 2F2 par; F1 aur 2F1 ke beech real, inverted enlarged image deta hai 2F2 se beyond; F1 par koi image nahi deta; F1 aur O ke beech virtual, erect, enlarged image deta hai object ke same side par.

Concave lens always virtual, erect aur diminished image deta hai, object position kuch bhi ho. Ray diagrams ke liye, principal axis ke parallel ray convex lens mein refraction ke baad F se pass hoti hai ya concave lens mein F se diverge hoti hui dikhti hai. F se pass hone wali ray principal axis ke parallel emerge hoti hai. Optical centre se pass hone wali ray bina deviation ke pass hoti hai.

sections.title: Lens formula, magnification, aur power
paragraphs: Lenses ke liye hum mirrors ke similar sign convention use karte hain, lekin saare measurements lens ke optical centre se liye jaate hain. Convex lens ki focal length positive hoti hai, aur concave lens ki focal length negative. u, v, f, object height h aur image height h' ke liye correct signs put karne ka dhyan rakhein.
Lens formula 1/v - 1/u = 1/f hai. Yeh general hai aur kisi bhi spherical lens ke liye sabhi situations mein valid hai. Lens ka magnification m = h'/h = v/u hota hai.

Lens ki power P = 1/f hoti hai. Iski SI unit dioptre hai, jise D se denote karte hain. Agar f metres mein hai, toh power dioptres mein hoti hai. Ek dioptre us lens ki power hai jiski focal length 1 metre hai, isliye 1 D = 1 m–1. Convex lens ki power positive hoti hai, aur concave lens ki power negative.

Kai optical instruments several lenses use karte hain. Contact mein rakhe lenses ke liye, net power individual powers ka algebraic sum hota hai: P = P1 + P2 + P3 + … . Example ke liye, +2.0 D power wala lens convex hai focal length +0.50 m ke saath, aur –2.5 D power wala lens concave hai focal length –0.40 m ke saath.

spec.question: Inmein se kaun sa statement plane mirror dwara banaye gaye image ko describe karta hai?
options: Yeh image virtual, erect hota hai, object ke same size ka hota hai, aur mirror ke peeche utni hi door hota hai jitna object mirror ke aage hota hai.
Yeh real, inverted aur enlarged hota hai.

paragraphs: Ek curved chamakdar surface, jaise ki chamach ki curved surface, curved mirror ki tarah act karti hai. Sabse common curved mirror spherical mirror hota hai, jiska reflecting surface sphere ke surface ka ek part banata hai. Agar reflecting surface andar ki taraf curved hai, to mirror concave mirror hota hai. Agar bahar ki taraf curved hai, to mirror convex mirror hota hai.

Reflecting surface ka centre pole P hota hai. Jis sphere ka mirror ek part banata hai, us sphere ka centre centre of curvature C hota hai; ye mirror ke bahar hota hai, concave mirror ke saamne aur convex mirror ke peeche. Us sphere ka radius radius of curvature R hota hai, aur distance (doori) PC equals R. P aur C se guzarne wali straight line principal axis hoti hai, aur ye P par mirror ke normal hoti hai. Reflecting surface ka diameter aperture hota hai. Hum un mirrors ko consider karte hain jinka aperture unke radius of curvature se bahut chhota hota hai.

Principal axis ke parallel rays concave mirror se reflection ke baad ek point par milti hain. Ye point principal focus F hota hai. Convex mirror mein reflected rays F se diverge hoti hui dikhti hain. P aur F ke beech ka distance focal length f hota hai. Chhote aperture wale spherical mirror ke liye, R = 2f, isliye F P aur C ke theek beech mein sthit hota hai.

Concave mirror ke liye, image object ki position par depend karti hai. Infinity par image F par real, inverted, highly diminished aur point-sized hoti hai. C ke beyond image F aur C ke beech real, inverted aur diminished hoti hai. C par image C par real, inverted aur same size ki hoti hai. C aur F ke beech image C ke beyond real, inverted aur enlarged hoti hai. F par koi image nahi banti. P aur F ke beech image mirror ke peeche virtual, erect aur enlarged hoti hai.

Convex mirror ke liye, infinity par object mirror ke peeche F par virtual, erect, highly diminished point-sized image deta hai. Infinity aur P ke beech ka object mirror ke peeche P aur F ke beech virtual, erect aur diminished image deta hai. Concave mirrors torches, search-lights, vehicle headlights, shaving mirrors mein, dentists dwara, aur solar furnaces mein use hote hain. Convex mirrors rear-view mirrors ke roop mein use hote hain kyunki ye erect, diminished image aur wider field of view dete hain.

spec.caption: Concave aur convex mirrors: P pole hai, C centre of curvature hai, F principal focus hai, R radius of curvature hai aur f focal length hai. Concave mirror ke liye C aur F mirror ke saamne hote hain; convex mirror ke liye ve mirror ke peeche hote hain.

spec.question: Ek spherical mirror ka radius of curvature 20 cm hai. Iski focal length cm mein kya hai?
spec.explanation: Chhote aperture ke spherical mirror ke liye, R = 2f. Isliye f = R/2 = 20 cm / 2 = 10 cm.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko R = 2f directly use karna chahiye.

spec.question: Aise mirror ka naam batao jo kisi object ka erect aur enlarged image bana sakta hai.
spec.answer: Concave mirror
spec.explanation: Jab object concave mirror ke pole aur principal focus ke beech hota hai, tab image virtual, erect aur enlarged hoti hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko concave mirror wala case yaad hona chahiye jisme virtual, erect aur enlarged image banti hai.

spec.question: Concave mirror ke principal focus ki definition do.
options: Principal axis par woh point jahan principal axis ke parallel rays reflection ke baad milte hain.
Us sphere ka centre jiska mirror ek part hai.
spec.answer: Principal axis par woh point jahan principal axis ke parallel rays reflection ke baad milte hain.
spec.explanation: Concave mirror ke liye, parallel rays reflection ke baad principal focus par converge hoti hain.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko principal focus ko pole, centre of curvature aur aperture se distinguish karna chahiye.

spec.question: Concave mirror se bani image virtual, erect aur object se badi observe hoti hai. Object ko kahan rakha jana chahiye?
options: Principal focus aur centre of curvature ke beech
Mirror ke pole aur principal focus ke beech
spec.answer: Mirror ke pole aur principal focus ke beech
spec.explanation: Concave mirror ke liye, virtual, erect aur enlarged image tab banti hai jab object P aur F ke beech hota hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko image description ko concave-mirror image table ki correct row se link karna chahiye.

spec.question: Hum ek concave mirror jiska focal length 15 cm hai, use karke erect image paana chahte hain. Object distance (doori) ki range kya honi chahiye aur image ki nature kya hogi?
options: C ke beyond; real, inverted, diminished
P aur F ke beech; virtual, erect, enlarged
C par; real, inverted, same size
C aur F ke beech; real, inverted, enlarged
spec.answer: P aur F ke beech; virtual, erect, enlarged
spec.explanation: Concave mirror se erect image virtual aur enlarged hoti hai, aur ye tab banti hai jab object pole aur principal focus ke beech rakha ho.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko pata hona chahiye ki concave mirror ka sirf wahi case erect image deta hai.

spec.question: In situations mein kaunsa type ka mirror use hota hai: (a) car ke headlights, (b) vehicle ka side/rear-view mirror, (c) solar furnace.
options: Headlights aur solar furnace ke liye concave; rear-view ke liye convex
Headlights aur solar furnace ke liye convex; rear-view ke liye concave
spec.answer: Headlights aur solar furnace ke liye concave; rear-view ke liye convex
spec.explanation: Concave mirrors headlights mein powerful parallel beams dete hain aur solar furnaces mein sunlight ko concentrate karte hain. Convex mirrors erect, diminished image aur rear-view use ke liye wider field of view dete hain.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko mirror type ko uske practical use se connect karna chahiye.

spec.question: Gaadiyon mein rear-view mirror ke liye hum convex mirror ko kyun prefer karte hain?
options: Yeh real aur enlarged image deta hai.
Yeh erect, diminished image aur wider field of view deta hai.
Yeh traffic ka inverted image deta hai.
Yeh object ke same size ka image deta hai.
spec.answer: Yeh erect, diminished image aur wider field of view deta hai.
spec.explanation: Convex mirror hamesha erect, diminished image deta hai aur outward curved hone ki wajah se plane mirror se zyada area dikhata hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko convex mirror ki image nature aur wide field of view dono yaad honi chahiye.

paragraphs: Ray diagram ki madad se aap image ka location bina har ray draw kiye pata kar sakte hain. Ek extended object ko kai point sources maana ja sakta hai, aur har point kai rays bhejta hai. Clarity ke liye, hum koi bhi do rays chunte hain jinki reflection ke baad direction aasani se pata ho. Jis point par kam se kam do reflected rays milti hain, ya milti hui lagti hain, wahi image position deta hai.

Concave mirror ke liye, principal axis ke parallel ek ray reflection ke baad F se guzarti hai. Convex mirror ke liye, wahi ray F se diverge hoti hui lagti hai. Concave mirror ke F se guzarne wali ray, ya convex mirror ke F ki taraf directed ray, reflection ke baad principal axis ke parallel nikalti hai.

Concave mirror ke C se guzarne wali ray, ya convex mirror ke C ki taraf directed ray, same path par wapas reflect hoti hai. Aisa isliye hota hai kyunki ray reflecting surface ke normal ke along padti hai. Pole P par obliquely incident ray obliquely reflect hoti hai, laws of reflection ka palan karte hue aur principal axis ke saath equal angles banati hai.

Har case mein, point of incidence par laws of reflection follow hote hain: angle of reflection, angle of incidence ke barabar hota hai. Aap in ray rules mein se koi bhi do use kar sakte hain diye gaye object position ke liye image draw karne ke liye.

spec.question: Concave mirror ke centre of curvature se pass hone wali ray reflect hokar kaise jaati hai?
options: Principal axis se 90° ke angle par
spec.answer: Usi path par wapas
spec.explanation: Ray point of incidence par reflecting surface ke normal ke along padti hai, isliye same path par wapas reflect hoti hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko centre-of-curvature ray rule yaad hona chahiye.

paragraphs: Mirror equations use karne ke liye, hum New Cartesian Sign Convention follow karte hain. Pole P origin hai, aur principal axis x-axis hai. Object hamesha mirror ke left side par rakha jaata hai, isliye light left se mirror par girti hai. P ke right side measure ki gayi distance (doori) positive hoti hai, aur left ki distance (doori) negative hoti hai. Principal axis ke upar measure ki gayi distance (doori) positive hoti hai, aur neeche wali negative hoti hai.

Object distance u hai, image distance v hai, aur focal length f hai. Mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f hai. Yeh sab situations mein, sab spherical mirrors ke liye aur sab object positions ke liye valid hai. Solve karne se pehle aapko u, v aur f ke signs sahi tarah put karne honge.

Magnification m batata hai ki image object ke comparison mein kitni badi hai. Yeh m = h'/h hai, jahan h object height hai aur h' image height hai. Yeh m = -v/u bhi hai. m ka negative value real image indicate karta hai, aur positive value virtual image indicate karta hai. Object ki height positive li jaati hai kyunki woh principal axis ke upar hai. Image height virtual image ke liye positive hoti hai aur real image ke liye negative hoti hai.

spec.problem: Ek automobile ke rear-view ke liye use hone wala convex mirror ki radius of curvature 3.00 m hai. Agar ek bus is mirror se 5.00 m par located hai, to image ki position, nature aur size find karo.

steps.title: Diye gaye values ko signs ke saath likho
steps.detail: R = +3.00 m. Object distance u = –5.00 m. Convex mirror ke liye principal focus mirror ke peeche hota hai, isliye f = R/2 = +3.00 m / 2 = +1.50 m.

steps.title: Magnification calculate karo
steps.detail: m = –v/u = –(1.15 m)/(–5.00 m) = +0.23. Positive m ka matlab virtual, erect image hai, aur size 0.23 ke factor se chhota hai.

spec.answer: Image mirror ke peeche 1.15 m par hai. Yeh virtual, erect hai aur object se 0.23 ke factor se chhota hai.

spec.problem: Ek object, jiska size 4.0 cm hai, focal length 15.0 cm wale concave mirror ke samne 25.0 cm par rakha gaya hai. Sharp image paane ke liye screen ko mirror se kitni distance par rakha jana chahiye? Image ki nature aur size find karo.

steps.title: Given values ko signs ke saath likho
steps.detail: Object height h = +4.0 cm. Object distance u = –25.0 cm. Concave mirror ke liye f = –15.0 cm. Humein v aur h' nikalna hai.

steps.title: v calculate karo
steps.detail: 1/v = (–5.0 + 3.0)/75.0 = –2.0/75.0, toh v = –37.5 cm. Screen ko mirror ke samne 37.5 cm par rakha jana chahiye. Image real hai.

steps.title: Image height calculate karo
steps.detail: m = h'/h = –v/u, toh h' = –v h/u = –(–37.5 cm)(+4.0 cm)/(–25.0 cm) = –6.0 cm. Image inverted aur enlarged hai.

spec.answer: Screen ko mirror ke samne 37.5 cm par rakha jana chahiye. Image real, inverted aur 6.0 cm tall hai, isliye ye enlarged hai.

spec.question: Ek convex mirror ki focal length find karo jiska radius of curvature 32 cm hai. Answer cm mein do.
spec.explanation: Chhote aperture wale spherical mirror ke liye, R = 2f. Isliye f = R/2 = 32 cm / 2 = 16 cm.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko convex mirror par bhi R = 2f apply karna chahiye.

spec.question: Ek concave mirror kisi object ka, jo uske saamne 10 cm par rakha hai, teen guna magnified real image banata hai. Image mirror se kitni door hai, cm mein?
spec.explanation: Real image ka magnification negative hota hai. m = –v/u = –3, jahan u = –10 cm. Isliye –v/(–10) = –3, yaani v = –30 cm. Image mirror ke saamne 30 cm par hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko real image ke liye magnification ka sign use karna aur v ke liye solve karna aana chahiye.

spec.question: Ek object convex mirror se 10 cm ki distance (doori) par rakha hai, jiska focal length 15 cm hai. Image distance cm mein find karo.
spec.explanation: u = –10 cm aur f = +15 cm leke 1/v + 1/u = 1/f use karo. 1/v = 1/15 + 1/10 = 1/6, isliye v = +6 cm. Image mirror ke peeche 6 cm par hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko convex mirror ke liye sahi positive focal length use karni chahiye.

spec.question: 7.0 cm size ka ek object concave mirror ke samne 27 cm par rakha gaya hai, jiska focal length 18 cm hai. Sharp focussed image paane ke liye screen ko mirror se kitni distance (doori) par, cm mein, rakha jaye?
spec.explanation: u = –27 cm, f = –18 cm. 1/v = 1/f – 1/u = –1/18 + 1/27 = –1/54, isliye v = –54 cm. Screen mirror ke samne 54 cm par rakhi jati hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko concave mirror ke liye mirror formula mein signs sahi tarah substitute karne chahiye.

paragraphs: Light ek transparent medium mein straight lines mein travel karti hai, lekin jab wo kisi doosre transparent medium mein obliquely enter karti hai to uski direction badal sakti hai. Is direction change ko refraction of light kehte hain. Iske examples tab dikhte hain jab pond ka bottom raised dikhta hai, glass slab ke neeche ke letters raised dikhte hain, paani mein partly doobi pencil displaced dikhti hai, aur paani mein rakha lemon sides se bigger dikhta hai.

Ek rectangular glass slab mein, light ray do surfaces par direction badalti hai. Air-glass surface par ye rarer medium se denser medium mein jaati hai aur normal ki taraf bend karti hai. Glass-air surface par ye denser medium se rarer medium mein jaati hai aur normal se away bend karti hai.

Emergent ray incident ray ke parallel hoti hai. Aisa isliye hota hai kyunki do opposite parallel faces par bending equal aur opposite hoti hai. Ray thodi sideward shift hoti hai, lekin uski direction original direction ke parallel hi rehti hai.

spec.question: Glass tumbler mein paani mein aadhi doobi pencil interface par displaced dikhti hai. Kyun?
options: Kyunki interface par light reflected hoti hai
Kyunki interface par light refracted hoti hai
Kyunki pencil paani mein actually bend hoti hai
Kyunki paani saari light absorb karta hai
spec.answer: Kyunki interface par light refracted hoti hai
spec.explanation: Paani ke andar wale pencil ke hisse se aap tak pahunchne wali light refraction ki wajah se alag direction se aati dikhti hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko refraction ke rozana ke examples identify karne chahiye.

spec.question: Rectangular glass slab se nikalne wale emergent ray ke baare mein kya sach hai?
options: Yeh incident ray ke perpendicular hota hai.
Yeh incident ray ke parallel hota hai aur sideward shifted hota hai.
Yeh permanently incident direction se away bend ho jata hai.
Yeh same path par wapas aa jata hai.
spec.answer: Yeh incident ray ke parallel hota hai aur sideward shifted hota hai.
spec.explanation: Do opposite parallel faces par bending equal aur opposite hoti hai, isliye emergent ray incident ray ke parallel hota hai lekin sideward shifted hota hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko glass-slab result yaad hona chahiye.

paragraphs: Refraction do laws ko follow karta hai. First, incident ray, refracted ray aur point of incidence par normal — ye sab same plane mein hote hain. Second, kisi given colour ke light aur given pair of media ke liye angle of incidence ke sine ka angle of refraction ke sine se ratio constant hota hai. Yahi Snell’s law hai, aur ye 0 < i < 90° ke liye true hai.

Is constant ko first medium ke respect mein second medium ka refractive index kaha jata hai. Agar light medium 1 se medium 2 mein jati hai, aur uski speed (chaal) v1 aur v2 hain, to n21 = v1/v2. Medium 2 ke respect mein medium 1 ka refractive index n12 = v2/v1 hota hai.

Agar medium 1 air ya vacuum hai, to refractive index ko absolute refractive index kaha jata hai. Ye n = c/v hai, jahan c air mein light ki speed hai aur v medium mein speed hai. Light vacuum mein sabse tez travel karti hai, jiski speed 3 × 10^8 m s–1 hai. Air mein ye sirf thodi hi kam hoti hai aur glass ya water mein kaafi kam ho jati hai.

Larger refractive index wala medium optically denser hota hai, aur lower refractive index wala medium optically rarer hota hai. Light rarer medium mein zyada tez chalti hai. Rarer se denser ki taraf jane wali ray slow ho jati hai aur normal ki taraf bend karti hai; denser se rarer ki taraf jane wali ray speed up ho jati hai aur normal se door bend karti hai. Optical density mass density ke same nahin hoti: kerosene ka refractive index water se higher hai, isliye ye water se optically denser hai, although iski mass density kam hai.

spec.question: Hawa mein chal rahi light ki ek ray tirchhi (obliquely) paani mein pravesh karti hai. Kya ye normal (abhilamb) ki taraf mudti hai ya normal se door, aur kyun?
options: Normal ki taraf, kyunki paani hawa se optically denser hai.
Normal se door, kyunki paani hawa se optically rarer hai.
Ye bina mude seedha chali jaati hai.
Ye normal ki taraf mudti hai kyunki paani ka refractive index kam hai.
spec.answer: Normal ki taraf, kyunki paani hawa se optically denser hai.
spec.explanation: Paani ka refractive index hawa se zyada hota hai, isliye ye optically denser hai. Rarer se denser medium mein jaane wali ray slow hoti hai aur normal ki taraf mudti hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko bending direction ko optical density se jodna chahiye.

spec.question: Light air se glass mein pravesh karti hai jiska refractive index 1.50 hai. Vacuum mein light ki speed (chaal) 3 × 10^8 m/s hai. Glass mein light ki speed m/s mein kya hai?
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko n = c/v use karna chahiye aur speed ko m/s mein hi rakhna chahiye.

spec.question: Refractive index table se, kaun sa medium sabse zyada optical density rakhta hai aur kaun sa sabse kam?
options: Diamond mein sabse zyada hai; air mein sabse kam hai.
Air mein sabse zyada hai; diamond mein sabse kam hai.
Water mein sabse zyada hai; kerosene mein sabse kam hai.
Crown glass mein sabse zyada hai; water mein sabse kam hai.
spec.answer: Diamond mein sabse zyada hai; air mein sabse kam hai.
spec.explanation: Diamond ka refractive index 2.42 hai, jo listed sabse bada hai, aur air ka 1.0003 hai, jo listed sabse chhota hai. Bada refractive index optically denser hone ka matlab hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko refractive index se optical density padhna aana chahiye.

spec.question: Aapko kerosene, turpentine aur water diye gaye hain. Inmein se kis mein light sabse tez travel karti hai?
spec.answer: Water
spec.explanation: Water ka refractive index in teeno mein sabse chhota hai (1.33, kerosene ke 1.44 aur turpentine ke 1.47 ke mukable), isliye light water mein sabse tez travel karti hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko refractive index aur speed ke beech inverse relation ka use karna chahiye.

spec.question: Diamond ka refractive index 2.42 hai. Is statement ka kya matlab hai?
options: Air mein light ki speed (chaal) aur diamond mein light ki speed ka ratio 2.42 hai, isliye diamond mein light dheemi hoti hai.
Diamond mein light ki speed (chaal) aur air mein light ki speed ka ratio 2.42 hai.
Light diamond mein air se zyada tez travel karti hai.
Diamond ki mass density air se 2.42 guna hai.
spec.answer: Air mein light ki speed (chaal) aur diamond mein light ki speed ka ratio 2.42 hai, isliye diamond mein light dheemi hoti hai.
spec.explanation: Absolute refractive index ke liye, n = c/v. Value 2.42 ka matlab hai ki c, diamond mein light ki speed (chaal) ka 2.42 guna hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko refractive-index value ko speed (chaal) ratio ke roop mein interpret karna chahiye.

paragraphs: A lens ek transparent material hai jo do surfaces se bound hota hai, jinme se ek ya dono spherical hote hain. Convex lens middle mein edges se thicker hota hai, aur light rays ko converge karta hai, isliye yeh converging lens hai. Concave lens edges par middle se thicker hota hai, aur light rays ko diverge karta hai, isliye yeh diverging lens hai.

Ek lens ke do centres of curvature C1 aur C2 hote hain. Principal axis in centres se pass karta hai. Lens ka central point optical centre O hai. O se pass hone wala ray bina deviation ke pass hota hai. Circular outline ka effective diameter aperture hai. Hum small apertures wale thin lenses consider karte hain.

Principal axis ke parallel rays convex lens se refraction ke baad principal focus par converge karte hain. Concave lens mein yeh same side par principal focus se diverge karte hue appear hote hain. Ek lens ke do principal foci F1 aur F2 hote hain, aur focal length f optical centre se principal focus ki distance (doori) hai. Lens aur Sun ke sharp image ke beech ki distance approximate focal length deti hai.

Convex lens ke liye image table yeh hai: object infinity par ho to F2 par real, inverted, highly diminished point-sized image milti hai; object 2F1 se aage ho to F2 aur 2F2 ke beech real, inverted, diminished image milti hai; object 2F1 par ho to 2F2 par real, inverted same-size image milti hai; object F1 aur 2F1 ke beech ho to 2F2 se aage real, inverted enlarged image milti hai; object F1 par ho to koi image nahi banti; object F1 aur O ke beech ho to object ke same side par virtual, erect, enlarged image milti hai.

Concave lens hamesha virtual, erect aur diminished image deta hai, object position koi bhi ho. Ray diagrams ke liye, principal axis ke parallel ray convex lens mein refraction ke baad F se pass hota hai ya concave lens mein F se diverge karta hua appear hota hai. F se pass hone wala ray principal axis ke parallel emerge hota hai. Optical centre se pass hone wala ray bina deviation ke pass hota hai.

spec.question: Nimnlikhit mein se kaun sa material lens banane ke liye use nahi kiya ja sakta?
spec.answer: Clay
spec.explanation: Lens ek transparent material se banta hai. Clay transparent nahi hota, isliye Clay se lens nahi bana sakte.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko yaad hona chahiye ki lens transparent hona chahiye.

spec.question: Aap dictionary mein mile chhote letters ko padhne ke liye kaun sa lens use karna pasand karenge?
spec.answer: Ek convex lens
spec.explanation: Ek convex lens virtual, erect aur enlarged image bana sakta hai jab object principal focus F1 aur optical centre O ke beech hota hai. Ek concave lens hamesha virtual, erect lekin diminished image deta hai, isliye yah letters ko enlarge nahi kar sakta.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko magnification ke liye converging lens chunna chahiye aur concave lens ko rule out karna chahiye, jo hamesha diminish karta hai.

spec.question: Convex lens ke saamne object ko kahan rakha jaye taaki object ke same size ka real image (vastavik pratibimb) mile?
options: Lens ke optical centre aur uske principal focus ke beech
spec.answer: Focal length ke twice par
spec.explanation: Convex lens ke liye, 2F1 par rakha object 2F2 par same size ka real, inverted image banata hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko convex-lens image table ki same-size row yaad honi chahiye.

spec.question: Ek concave lens ka use karke kisi object ko dekha jata hai. Bane hue image (pratibimb) ki nature kya hai?
spec.answer: Virtual, erect aur diminished
spec.explanation: Concave lens hamesha virtual, erect aur diminished image deta hai, chahe object ki position koi bhi ho.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko yaad rakhna chahiye ki concave lens ka image kabhi real ya enlarged nahi hota, object ki position kuch bhi ho.

paragraphs: Lenses ke liye hum mirrors jaise sign convention ka use karte hain, lekin saare measurements lens ke optical centre se liye jaate hain. Convex lens ki focal length positive hoti hai, aur concave lens ki focal length negative hoti hai. Dhyan rakhein ki u, v, f, object height h aur image height h' ke liye sahi signs lagayein.
Lens formula 1/v - 1/u = 1/f hai. Ye general hai aur kisi bhi spherical lens ke liye har situation mein valid hai. Lens ka magnification m = h'/h = v/u hota hai.

Lens ki power P = 1/f hoti hai. Iska SI unit dioptre hai, jise D se denote karte hain. Agar f metres mein hai, to power dioptres mein hoti hai. Ek dioptre us lens ki power hai jiski focal length 1 metre hai, isliye 1 D = 1 m–1. Convex lens ki power positive hoti hai, aur concave lens ki power negative hoti hai.

Kai optical instruments kai lenses ka use karte hain. Ek doosre ke contact mein rakhe gaye lenses ke liye net power individual powers ka algebraic sum hota hai: P = P1 + P2 + P3 + … . Example ke liye, +2.0 D power wala lens convex hai jiski focal length +0.50 m hai, aur –2.5 D power wala lens concave hai jiski focal length –0.40 m hai.

spec.problem: Ek concave lens ki focal length 15 cm hai. Object ko lens se kis distance (doori) par rakha jaaye taaki wo lens se 10 cm par image banaye? Saath hi, lens dwara produce magnification bhi find karein.

steps.title: Diye gaye values signs ke saath likhein
steps.detail: Concave lens hamesha object ke same side par virtual, erect image banata hai. Image distance v = –10 cm; focal length f = –15 cm; object distance u = ?

steps.title: u calculate karein
steps.detail: 1/u = (–3 + 2)/30 = –1/30, isliye u = –30 cm. Object distance 30 cm hai.

steps.title: Magnification calculate karein
steps.detail: m = v/u = (–10 cm)/(–30 cm) = +1/3 = +0.33. Positive sign dikhata hai ki image erect aur virtual hai. Image object size ka one-third hai.

spec.answer: Object lens se 30 cm door hai. Magnification +0.33 hai, isliye image virtual, erect aur object size ka one-third hai.

spec.problem: 2.0 cm tall object ko convex lens ke principal axis ke perpendicular rakha gaya hai; lens ki focal length 10 cm hai. Object ki lens se distance (doori) 15 cm hai. Image ki nature, position aur size find karein. Uska magnification bhi find karein.

steps.title: Given values ko signs ke saath likhein
steps.detail: Object height h = +2.0 cm; focal length f = +10 cm; object distance (doori) u = –15 cm; image distance v = ?; image height h' = ?

steps.title: v calculate karein
steps.detail: 1/v = (3 – 2)/30 = 1/30, isliye v = +30 cm. Image optical centre ke doosri side 30 cm par hai. Image real aur inverted hai.

steps.title: Image height aur magnification calculate karein
steps.detail: m = h'/h = v/u, isliye h' = h(v/u) = 2.0 × (+30/–15) = –4.0 cm. Saath hi m = v/u = +30/–15 = –2. Negative signs dikhate hain ki image inverted aur real hai.

spec.answer: Image lens ke doosri side 30 cm par banti hai. Ye real, inverted aur 4.0 cm tall hai, isliye ye two times enlarged hai.

spec.problem: 5 cm length ka ek object 10 cm focal length ke converging lens se 25 cm door rakha gaya hai. Image ki position, size aur nature find karein.

steps.title: Given values ko signs ke saath likhein
steps.detail: Object height h = +5 cm; object distance u = –25 cm; converging (convex) lens ke liye focal length f = +10 cm. Humein v aur h' nikalna hai.

steps.title: v calculate karein
steps.detail: 1/v = (5 – 2)/50 = 3/50, isliye v = +50/3 cm ≈ 16.7 cm. Image lens ke doosri side par hai aur real hai.

steps.title: Image height calculate karein
steps.detail: m = v/u = (50/3)/(–25) = –2/3. Phir h' = h × m = 5 × (–2/3) ≈ –3.3 cm. Image inverted aur diminished hai.

spec.answer: Image lens se doosri side par lagbhag 16.7 cm door hai. Yeh real, inverted aur lagbhag 3.3 cm tall hai, isliye diminished hai.

spec.question: 15 cm focal length ka ek concave lens lens se 10 cm door image banata hai. Object lens se kitni door rakha gaya hai, cm mein?
spec.explanation: v = –10 cm aur f = –15 cm leke 1/v – 1/u = 1/f use karein. 1/u = 1/v – 1/f = –1/10 + 1/15 = –1/30, isliye u = –30 cm. Object lens se 30 cm door hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko concave lens ke liye negative signs ke saath lens formula use karna chahiye.

spec.question: Power –2.0 D wale lens ka focal length aur type find karo.
spec.answer: f = –0.50 m; concave lens
spec.explanation: P = 1/f, isliye f = 1/P = 1/(–2.0) m = –0.50 m. Negative power ka matlab concave lens hota hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko power ko focal length mein convert karna aur sign se lens type identify karna aana chahiye.

spec.question: Ek doctor ne +1.5 D power ka corrective lens prescribe kiya hai. Iska focal length aur type kya hai?
spec.answer: f = +0.67 m; converging lens
spec.explanation: f = 1/P = 1/1.5 m ≈ +0.67 m. Positive power ka matlab convex, converging lens hota hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko P = 1/f use karna aur positive power ka interpretation karna aana chahiye.

spec.question: Lens ki power ke 1 dioptre ko define karein.
options: 1 dioptre un lens ki power hai jiska focal length 1 metre hai.
1 dioptre un lens ka focal length hai jiski power 1 metre hai.
1 dioptre un lens ki power hai jiska focal length 1 cm hai.
spec.answer: 1 dioptre un lens ki power hai jiska focal length 1 metre hai.
spec.explanation: Power ka SI unit dioptre hai, aur 1 D = 1 m–1.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko dioptre ki definition batani chahiye.

spec.question: Ek concave lens (avatal lens) ki power dioptres mein nikalein jiska focal length 2 m hai.
spec.explanation: P = 1/f = 1/(–2 m) = –0.5 D. Negative sign se pata chalta hai ki lens concave hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko concave lens ke liye negative sign lagana chahiye.

spec.question: Ek convex lens (utal lens) ek needle ka real aur inverted image usse 50 cm ki doori (distance) par banata hai. Image object ke size ke barabar hai. Needle kahan rakhi hai, aur lens ki power kya hai?
spec.answer: Object 50 cm par; power +4 D
spec.explanation: Convex lens real aur same-size image deta hai jab object 2F par aur image 2F par hoti hai. Kyunki v = 50 cm, f = 25 cm = 0.25 m. Object bhi 50 cm par hai. Power P = 1/f = 1/0.25 = +4 D.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko same-size image condition ko lens formula aur power ke saath combine karna chahiye.

spec.question: Ek plane mirror (samtal darpan) ka magnification +1 hai. Iska kya matlab hai?
options: Image height object height ke barabar hai, aur image virtual aur erect hai.
Image object ke comparison mein enlarged hai.
spec.answer: Image height object height ke barabar hai, aur image virtual aur erect hai.
spec.explanation: Magnification m = h'/h hota hai. +1 value ka matlab hai h' equals h, isliye image ka size object ke barabar hai. m ki positive value virtual image ko indicate karti hai, aur plane mirror (samtal darpan) ki image virtual aur erect hoti hai.
spec.expected_understanding: Students ko magnification +1 ko 'same size' ke roop mein padhna chahiye aur positive sign ko virtual image se connect karna chahiye.
